transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-12-23 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (AetherWorks CTO), Diego Ramos (Platform), Samir Patel (Security), Priya Kapoor (ML)
Links shared: deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/integration-overview, security packet link: https://redwood.ai/security/sales-packet.pdf, example repo: (will be shared)

Summary note: auto-gen summary may be slightly off; see full transcript.

[00:00] Nina Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining on a friday afternoon, i'm nina from redwood inference, and with me is marcus our se. quick intro around who you are from aetherworks?
[00:08] Laura Chen: hi all laura here, cto at aetherworks. we run a search/assistant product for developer docs, looking to move some of our serving off our self-hosted cluster into a managed inference platform or a hybrid setup.
[00:18] Diego Ramos: diego - infra/platform, mostly care about the network, burst patterns, and how we'd run a gateway in front of things.
[00:24] Samir Patel: samir security, i'll be focused on kms, audit logs, and sso.
[00:29] Nina Patel: great, thanks. marcus do you want to kick off on the integration patterns we typically see?
[00:34] Marcus Lee: yeah for sure. so we typically see three patterns: direct sdk calls to hosted endpoints, a gateway/proxy sidecar that centralizes auth, rate limiting and caching, and finally a private deployment (vpc or on-prem) where the control plane is managed but the inference is in your network. we'll go through pros/cons and sample configs.
[00:50] Marcus Lee: one quick note on vocab i might say kv cache as K-V cash in the transcript so apologies, and lang chain sometimes becomes lang chain.
[00:58] Laura Chen: the main constraints for us are: bursty developer traffic -- big spikes when docs go viral -- and strict data residency and kms separation for some customers. also want to instrument costs at token level to charge back to teams.
[01:12] Diego Ramos: and we have a homegrown gateway that applies auth and throttling, curious how redwood's gateway plays with our existing proxy. would we run redwood behind our gateway or vice versa?
[01:22] Marcus Lee: good question. both are possible. common approach: keep your edge gateway and put a lightweight redwood sidecar or proxy that handles retryable semantics, prefix caching and batching; or route to redwood's gateway and use your gateway for perimeter auth. depends on where you want rate-limit enforcement.
[01:35] Laura Chen: if we keep our gateway in front, can we still get token-level cost data and traces per request? that's critical.
[01:42] Nina Patel: yes - we emit tracing hooks and support open telemetry. the SDKs (python/node) include optional callback hooks that forward token/billing metadata to your observability stack. marcus can you share example?
[01:52] Marcus Lee: i have a quick snippet i'll send; basically there's a middleware you can drop in that attaches request_id, model_version, tokens_generated and latency. with our console you can also map routes to cost buckets.
[02:06] Diego Ramos: how heavy is the sidecar in terms of cpu? our nodes are tight.
[02:11] Marcus Lee: very lightweight for proxy-only use, it's mostly io bound; the heavier parts (batching, kv cache) can be offloaded to a dedicated pool if you want. for hosted endpoints we manage those pools.
[02:24] Priya Kapoor: on the ml side, we use langchain and some llama index embeddings heavy workflows. how are embeddings and retrieval-augmented-generation handled? any native connectors?
[02:33] Marcus Lee: we have first-class SDK samples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. for embeddings there's a dedicated embeddings endpoint and we support synchronous and async calls. the patterns we recommend are: compute embeddings in a batch job or stream them, store in your vector db, and at query time use our small-context streaming to fetch KV cache hits.
[02:52] Priya Kapoor: do you have a code example for streaming with LangChain agents?
[02:56] Marcus Lee: yes, i'll push a playground example - it shows the callback integration for agent steps.
[03:02] Samir Patel: security wise, we need to know about key management - can we bring our own keys (HSM/KMS)? and audit logs must be paper-trail-able for SOC2.
[03:12] Nina Patel: you can bring your own KMS in Private deployments; for Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. Hosted also supports envelope encryption and customer-managed keys for certain enterprise tiers. audit logs are exportable; we keep token-level metadata and request/response hashes for retention policies.
[03:30] Diego Ramos: about quotas - we already enforce per-team quotas, do you support per-token quotas and soft throttles?
[03:38] Marcus Lee: yes, quotas can be defined per API key, per route, or per team via our console. soft throttles are available and can return retry-after headers. we also support dynamic quota policies that change during burst windows.
[03:51] Laura Chen: latency is also a big factor - for interactive use we need p95 < 220ms for short prompts. do you have benchmarks for hosted endpoints?
[03:59] Nina Patel: our published benchmarks are on the catalog; for small models we hit sub-200ms on optimized hardware. we'll coordinate a small perf run with your sample traffic to validate.
[04:10] Priya Kapoor: do you do automatic quantization recommendations? we worry about hallucination regression when quantizing.
[04:18] Marcus Lee: Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles and we surface expected quality deltas. for production-critical flows we recommend A/B with a canary rollout and compare eval prompts.
[04:33] Diego Ramos: on network topology, if we go private (vpc peering) what are the egress patterns? bandwith costs?
[04:41] Nina Patel: depends on whether you use our private package or an on-prem bundle. VPC peering keeps traffic in region; we provide snapshot guidance on egress. we can share a cost calc for your egress numbers.
[04:52] Samir Patel: what about identity - SSO, SAML, RBAC?
[04:56] Marcus Lee: SSO and SAML are supported; for finer role-based access we support RBAC with route-level permissions and token scoping.
[05:05] Laura Chen: can we session-record request/response for auditing? storing full responses may be sensitive.
[05:12] Nina Patel: you can configure redaction rules and store hashed response digests for audit, or store full payloads in Private deployments if policies allow.
[05:23] Diego Ramos: one of our ops constraints is burst concurrency: spikes of concurrent short requests (500-1k) for short periods - how does redwood handle queueing vs rejecting?
[05:33] Marcus Lee: we have configurable burst windows and autoscale policies; you can opt for queueing up to a soft window with progressive rejection. for guaranteed SLAs Dedicated reserved capacity is recommended.
[05:45] Laura Chen: what's the migration path: start hosted then move to dedicated? or test private first?
[05:51] Nina Patel: many customers start hosted for speed, then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and Dedicated/private for regulatory needs. we support pinning model versions to avoid drift.
[05:59] Priya Kapoor: for LangChain connectors if we do agentic workflows that call external tools, is there any function-calling or tool invocation support?
[06:07] Marcus Lee: yes we support function/tool calling semantics and structured output. SDKs include the function schema helpers that map to LangChain function calling patterns.
[06:18] Laura Chen: can you talk through an example gateway config for hybrid: our edge gateway -> redwood sidecar -> redwood hosted endpoint. what headers should we pass?
[06:28] Marcus Lee: pass x-request-id, authorization (api key or signed token), x-team-id and any tenant metadata. the sidecar can attach routing hints like preferred-region and caching keys. we'll send a sample proxy config.
[06:42] Diego Ramos: about quotas again - do quotas apply across gateway proxies? we have multiple frontends.
[06:48] Marcus Lee: quotas can be enforced centrally at the control plane by API key, so if your frontends share keys you get aggregated quotas. alternatively per-route keys give per-front-end quotas.
[06:59] Samir Patel: regulatory question - customers in EU require data residency and specific audit trails; can you guarantee that for hosted?
[07:07] Nina Patel: we have region-specific hosted zones and can guarantee no cross-region data movement for enterprise tiers. for strict residency we recommend Private.
[07:15] Laura Chen: ok let's talk deliverables - we want to run a 2-week pilot on hosted with 3 routes: embeddings, chat, and rerank. what instrumentation should we add?
[07:27] Marcus Lee: instrument request_id, route_name, model_version, tokens_in/tokens_out, and latency. add eval prompts for quality monitoring and set up alerts in the console. we'll provide a sample instrumentation guide.
[07:42] Nina Patel: we'll share a sample LangChain integration repo, proxy config, and a sandbox api key with restricted quotas.
[07:51] Diego Ramos: what about client SDKs - do they support automatic reconnects and streaming semantics? our mobile clients need long lived streams.
[07:59] Marcus Lee: yes, SDK streaming uses chunked responses and supports reconnect/resume for short interruptions. mobile usage considerations: use smaller chunk windows.
[08:11] Laura Chen: concerning costs - per-token pricing is fine but we need predictable monthly commits for peak. how do you do reserved capacity?
[08:20] Nina Patel: Dedicated reserved capacity is committed monthly/annually and gives throughput guarantees and lower per-token pricing for sustained usage. We also support burst pools on top.
[08:33] Priya Kapoor: any known pitfalls integrating with LlamaIndex?
[08:37] Marcus Lee: mostly around embedding dimension mismatches and async batching - our SDKs include helpers to normalize embeddings and batch them to the embeddings endpoint.
[08:44] Laura Chen: what telemetry do we get on the console? per-route, per-token cost, p95/p99, traces, and error rates?
[08:52] Marcus Lee: all of the above; plus you can instrument custom tags to group by feature.
[08:59] Samir Patel: if we need SOC2 type documents, what's the turnaround?
[09:03] Nina Patel: we can share our SOC2 summary and some artifact evidence within 2 business days; full SOC2 report is available under NDA.
[09:12] Diego Ramos: do you support bringing your own vector DB or do you prefer using embedded vector store?
[09:18] Marcus Lee: bring your own vector DB is common; we integrate with Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, and customers' self-hosted stores. we also offer managed vector store as an optional service.
[09:29] Laura Chen: for the pilot, how do we handle secrets rotation and api key management?
[09:35] Nina Patel: keys are manageable in the console with rotation policies; for Private we integrate with your KMS and don't store plaintext keys.
[09:44] Priya Kapoor: small question: does the sdk expose re-ranking helpers?
[09:48] Marcus Lee: yes there's a helper lib to batch rerank calls and return position scores.
[09:54] Laura Chen: any red flags or gotchas we should know before starting pilot?
[09:58] Marcus Lee: mainly to baseline current token counts and add instrumentation early; also test for cold-start on KV cache.
[10:07] Nina Patel: ok time to recap and next steps. we'll share three artifacts: integration example repo (LangChain + proxy), proxy config doc, and a pilot instrumentation checklist. SE will run a follow-up 1-hr dedicated session to talk cost modeling.
[10:25] Laura Chen: sounds good, i'm comfortable starting hosted pilot. we'll try to hand over sample traffic by monday.
[10:31] Diego Ramos: i'll send our rate-limit config and ingress patterns.
[10:34] Samir Patel: i'll list compliance doc requirements.
[10:37] Nina Patel: great - thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the repo and calendar invites. happy holidays.
[10:44] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hear of acronyms (KMS -> K-M-S, KV cache -> K-V cash), speaker interruptions, some filler 'uh' and 'um' removed in places for readability.
